newsitem.title: MEXICO: Five surviving Mexican septuplets struggle on.
newsitem.headline: Five surviving Mexican septuplets struggle on.

text.p: Five surviving Mexican septuplets battled to stay alive on Monday but doctors said one girl was in serious risk of dying, as two of her infant sisters did last weekend.

Fernando Rios Montiel, a doctor overseeing the five in intensive therapy in a Mexico City hospital, said one of the infants was in the most serious condition, and was struggling to breathe. She weighed 23.1 ounces (660 grams).
Her parents have baptised the five children, and Television Azteca showed a single cot prepared for their homecoming in the humble home where the couple lives.

"I told them to fight, I want them home," said their 28-year-old mother, Maria Rocio Diaz Carrillo, who gave birth to the five girls and two boys 12 weeks prematurely on Jan 21. She had taken fertility medicine after trying to get pregnant for five years.
